ai.description: *Minervarya gomantaki* is a small frog (25–35 mm) with a brown-mottled dorsum and white belly. It is distinguished by a prominent, dark-edged glandular fold and a distinct, pale mid-dorsal stripe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya gomantaki* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold running along the edge of its lower jaw.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya gomantaki* inhabits moist deciduous forests and agricultural landscapes in the Western Ghats, typically found near water bodies at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Goan Fejervarya is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates along the edges of paddy fields and seasonal water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya gomantaki* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in shallow water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya gomantaki* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Goa and Karnataka at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya gomantaki* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched metallic chirps, typically heard from flooded paddy fields and marshes.
